title: Runtime throughput vs latency vs cost — console vignette (draft)
content:
Purpose
This is a short, portable vignette intended for the Console team: a concise narrative + ascii charts to help product and SRE teams reason about throughput/latency/cost tradeoffs when exposing autoscale and batching knobs in the UI. The goal is a copyable help-snippet for the Console rollout docs and a reference for a quick demo.

Scope and audience
- Audience: product PMs, console UX engineers, SRE on-call, solutions eng.
- Scope: single-model serving profile (Llama2-70B-like), two hardware tiers (edge A100-ish vs core H100-ish), sessionized traffic (chat sessions), mix of short and long turns. This is intentionally small-scope — not a canonical lab benchmark.

Measurement setup (brief)
- Synthetic driver: 200 clients, Poisson arrivals, session length distribution: 60% short (<40 tokens), 40% long (>=200 tokens).
- Model config: FP16 quantized variant with KV-cache enabled.
- Hardware: "edge" 1xA100-40GB, "core" 2xH100-80GB.
- Key metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms per response), tokens/sec throughput, GPU-util, cost-per-1000-tokens (est USD from infra price table).
- Duration: 30 minute sustained run with 3x 5-minute burst windows.

Narrative findings (high level)
1) For session-heavy short-turn workloads, small batching windows (20–50ms) produce large throughput gains without visible p95 tail degradation. This is the sweet spot the Console should expose as "interactive batching".
2) For long-turn dominated workloads, larger batching (100–200ms) improves unit cost but increases p95 significantly; expose as "batch mode" with explicit SLO warnings.
3) Cold-penalties and start-up handshake (session context restoration) create a ~12–18% effective cost tax unless prefix/KV cache hit rates are >65%. Console should surface cache-hit and warm-pool metrics next to cost estimates.

ASCII charts and compact visuals
1) Latency vs batching window (edge/core) — p95 (ms) vs batching window (ms)

Batch(ms) | edge_p95(ms) | core_p95(ms)
------------------------------------
0         |  120         |  95
20        |  135         |  102
50        |  160         |  125
100       |  260         |  210
200       |  480         |  360

Interpretation: Small windows add modest p95 on edge but core is flatter due to better kernel parallelism. Beyond ~100ms window latency cost explodes for interactive flows.

2) Cost-per-1k-tokens (USD) vs throughput mode
Mode          | tokens/sec | cost_per_1k
---------------------------------------
interactive   |  900       |  0.085
balanced      |  1400      |  0.062
batch         |  2400      |  0.038

Interpretation: Moving from interactive to batch nearly triples tokens/sec and halves cost-per-token compared to balanced. But p95 in batch is >3x interactive.

3) Burst window behaviour (30s bursts) — p99 tail shift (ms)
Time offset (s) | p99_before | p99_during_burst | p99_after
-------------------------------------------------------
-30             |  720       |  ---             |  ---
0               |  700       |  1400            |  1100
+30             |  680       |  1250            |  900

Note: p99 spikes during burst and remains elevated for ~30–60s due to preemption/backfilling overheads. Console should surface an "expected tail during bursts" callout.

Short recommendations for Console (copyable)
- Expose 2 high-level modes: Interactive (low batching, prioritized scheduling) and Cost-Efficient (larger batching, opportunistic slots). Provide an inline SLO slider that maps to the backend presets below.
- Show estimated cost-per-1k-tokens and expected p95/p99 with confidence bands (derived from recent 24h telemetry).
- Add a small badge: "expected burst tail: +X% p99 for first Ys" when autoscale policies allow preemption.
- Surface KV cache hit % and warm-pool size in the routing tab — these are highly predictive of effective cost.

Preset mapping (suggested backend knobs)
- Interactive: batching_window_ms=30, preempt_priority=high, warm_pool=1.5x steady, routing_policy=latency-first
- Balanced: batching_window_ms=80, preempt_priority=medium, warm_pool=1.1x, routing_policy=cost-weighted latency-softcap
- Cost-Efficient: batching_window_ms=180, preempt_priority=low, warm_pool=0.6x, routing_policy=cost-first

UX microcopy suggestions
- Tooltip for batching: "Batching groups nearby requests for higher throughput. Larger batching saves money but may increase tail latency for interactive users."
- KV cache tooltip: "Prefix/KV cache stores recent session context. Higher hit rates reduce token compute and improve latency."
- Burst badge: "During sudden spikes we expect a temporary increase in worst-case latency — consider raising warm-pool to reduce this."

Methodology caveats and open questions
- This vignette is based on a single-model family and two representative instance classes; numbers should not be treated as product guarantees.
- Need more runs with our 2-phase traffic generator (real user traces replay) to validate burst recovery times.
- Missing: multi-tenant interference tests (noisy neighbor) — crucial for Dedicated.

Next steps (owner: eng-console)
- Run three repeat experiments using real trace replay and add 95% confidence intervals to cost and latency numbers (owner: Arjun) — due 2026-09-09.
- Prototype inline cost estimator in Console UI using these presets + live 24h telemetry (owner: Lina) — prototype by 2026-09-20.
- Add a small SLO demo script for Solutions Eng showing how to trade p95 vs cost for a specific customer profile (owner: Owen) — draft by 2026-09-15.

End.
